acceptance: A bundle from any run carries the start and end samples from the existing snapshot code; where load average is unavailable the field is null, not absent, and a test covers that case.
Sampling stays outside every measured interval; the PR shows where the start sample is taken and that power-test query timings are unchanged.
Smoke: two scale 0.01 runs through make heavy-run, one on a quiet host and one beside a deliberate CPU load, show clearly different recorded values.
The submission validator, the corpus inventory generator and the Explorer build accept bundles with and without the new fields, and the artifact privacy check passes.
The schema version changes as benchbox/core/results/schema_policy.py requires for an additive field, the result-format documentation lists the fields, and a changelog.d fragment is present.
The external soundness review of the PR head is resolved before merge.

description:
Problem: a run already samples load average, CPU frequency, available memory and swap (the resource snapshot in benchbox/platforms/base/result_capture.py), but the bundle writer in benchbox/core/results/schema.py drops it: none of the published bundles contains a load average. A bundle from a busy host therefore looks the same as one from an idle host. A person usually knows what else was running; an agent sharing a host with other agents does not.

Outcome: the existing end-of-run snapshot is written into the bundle's environment block, and a matching sample is taken at run start. Values a platform cannot report are an explicit null. The integrity validator reports them as INFO.

Non-goals: no threshold, no warning level, no refusal to run, no calibration workload, and no second sampler beside the existing one.
